login_with_jwt.note: M2M client_credentials grant. grant_type MUST be 'client_credentials'. Requires a MachineToMachine application.

create_provider.note: Creates an enterprise SSO connector (SAML or OIDC). providerName: 'SAML' or 'OIDC'. config contains IdP metadata/endpoints.

create_application.note: type MUST be one of: Native, SPA, Traditional, MachineToMachine, Protected, SAML. postLogoutRedirectUris MUST be an array (can be empty []).

update_application.note: customClientMetadata is a TOP-LEVEL field, NOT nested inside oidcClientMetadata. app_id in path must match the captured id from create_application.

login_with_password.note: Logto uses the Experience API for password login. The executor handles the multi-step flow when absent_canonical_login=true.

saml_login.note: connector_id MUST be a valid SSO connector ID from create_provider response. Use the captured connector_id, not a placeholder.

metadata.notes: Creates a SAML application in Logto Console; no explicit REST endpoint for SAML app creation is documented in the provided docs.

oidc_jwt.description: When no resource is specified, Logto may issue an opaque access token instead of a JWT. This token is intended for /oidc/me and introspection-based use cases.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag missing JWT claims/audience as a broker bug when the client omitted resource and received an opaque token by design.

oidc_jwt.description: Existing JWTs keep their old scopes until expiration even after permissions are reduced; only newly issued tokens reflect downscoped permissions.
oidc_jwt.note: A stale old token retaining prior scopes is by design; only a newly issued token should be used to test propagation.

oidc_jwt.description: For global API resources, newly granted permissions do not appear through refresh unless they were part of the original requested scope set; a new authorization flow may be required.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag absence of newly granted scopes in refreshed tokens as a bug if those scopes were not originally requested.

oidc_jwt.description: Organization tokens are not fetched directly from the authorization code flow; user flows must use refresh token flow to obtain organization tokens.
oidc_jwt.note: A missing organization token directly after code exchange is expected behavior, not a failure of organization authorization.

oidc_jwt.description: Permission changes do not modify existing JWTs. Newly issued tokens reflect downscoped permissions immediately, while enlarged permissions may require a new authorization flow if they exceed the originally requested scopes.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not treat old tokens retaining old scopes until expiry as stale-cache vulnerability by itself.

oidc_jwt.description: Permission changes are reflected only in newly issued JWTs; existing JWTs retain old scopes until expiration.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not treat old-token access after admin changes as stale-cache vulnerability unless a newly issued token also ignores the change.

oidc_jwt.description: Enterprise SSO identities are automatically linked to an existing user account when the working email matches an existing Logto user.
oidc_jwt.note: Identity merge by matching email is documented behavior; do not treat same downstream account for email-matching SSO as an unexpected collision.

oidc_jwt.description: After admin rotates OIDC signing keys, new tokens are expected to be signed by the new key immediately in Cloud, while previously signed tokens may remain valid until normal token/grant expiry unless separately revoked.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag acceptance of newly signed tokens after admin rotation as a vulnerability; only continued acceptance of old trust after explicit invalidation/expiry should be tested.

oidc_jwt.description: Admin-initiated signing key rotation authorizes a new trust anchor. New keys taking effect after rotation are expected behavior.
oidc_jwt.note: Only acceptance of old keys after explicit rotation should be investigated; acceptance of new keys is by design.

oidc_jwt.description: After signing key rotation, Cloud tenants apply the new signing key immediately; previous keys remain valid for already issued tokens until removed.
oidc_jwt.note: Admin-authorized trust anchor rotation is by design. Only acceptance of removed/old keys after intended retirement should be treated as suspicious.

oidc_jwt.description: When no resource is specified, Logto issues an opaque access token instead of a JWT. This token is intended for userinfo and general purposes and must be validated via introspection rather than local JWT verification.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag lack of JWT claims/audience fields as a bug when the client omitted resource.

oidc_jwt.description: End-session clears the centralized Logto session, but grants with offline_access are not revoked by default and can remain valid until grant TTL expiry.
oidc_jwt.note: A refresh-capable grant surviving browser sign-out is documented behavior, not automatic replay vulnerability.

oidc_jwt.description: If direct sign-in fails because the connector is not found or not enabled, Logto falls back to the standard sign-in page.
oidc_jwt.note: This is expected UX fallback, not flow confusion.

oidc_jwt.constraint: Logto issues opaque access tokens when no resource is specified in the authorization or token request. For oidc_jwt tests that require JWT claim inspection or audience validation, the fuzzer MUST include a resource parameter (or rely on a configured default API resource). Otherwise verify_granted_identity via /oidc/me may still work, but JWT-specific invariants will be untestable because the access token is opaque.

Default API resource behavior changes token format: if resource is omitted and no default API resource is configured, Logto may issue an opaque token; if a default API resource is configured and openid is not included, Logto issues a JWT for that default audience. The fuzzer MUST control resource and scope explicitly and MUST NOT infer JWT-vs-opaque behavior from omission alone.

For I1/I5 audience-binding tests, the resource parameter must exactly match the registered API identifier (resource indicator URI). Logto does exact string matching; prefixes, shortened names, or partial matches are not wildcards. For multi-audience scenarios, request the exact target resource URI each time.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, include a control token request/login in the same run using a valid token configuration. A failed protected-resource call without a control cannot distinguish invalid token handling from broken client/app/resource setup.

Logto validation examples often set verify_aud=false in JWT libraries and require applications to verify audience manually based on permission model. Therefore, any I1/I5 audience test against a Logto-protected API MUST implement explicit audience checks in the test resource or oracle; relying on library defaults may produce false positives because issuer/signature can pass while audience is unchecked.

For organization-scoped JWT tests, the fuzzer MUST include organization_id in the token request. Without organization_id, Logto evaluates only global roles/permissions and organization RBAC is not enforced. A missing organization_id can make cross-org or org-permission tests pass or fail for the wrong reason.

Organization tokens cannot be fetched directly from the authorization code flow. To test organization JWTs for user flows, the fuzzer MUST first obtain a refresh token, then call /oidc/token with grant_type=refresh_token plus organization parameters. Treat direct auth-code acquisition of organization tokens as unsupported, not a security failure.

Permission changes are reflected only in newly issued JWTs; existing JWTs keep old scopes until expiry. For I3 config-tightening or permission-change tests, the fuzzer MUST obtain a NEW token after the change and MUST NOT expect an already-issued JWT to shrink in place.

For global API resources, enlarged permissions do NOT appear through refresh unless they were part of the original requested scope set. To test I5 scope escalation correctly, the fuzzer MUST distinguish 'newly granted but not originally requested' from 'improperly over-issued'. A token containing scopes outside the original request set is suspicious; absence of newly granted scopes after refresh is by design.

For organization tokens, enlarged permissions can appear on next issuance (refresh or token request), but still only within the originally requested scope set unless a new authorization flow is performed. The fuzzer MUST keep the original requested scopes fixed when testing post-change behavior.

Token exchange is disabled by default per application. Before any RFC 8693 test, the target application MUST have 'Allow token exchange' enabled; otherwise 'token exchange is not allowed for this application' is expected and is not evidence of secure audience enforcement.

For PAT-based token exchange, subject_token_type must be exactly urn:logto:token-type:personal_access_token. For impersonation-style token exchange, subject_token_type is urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token. The fuzzer MUST use the documented exact token type string; mismatched token types cause expected rejection and are not security findings.

Logto token exchange uses the same /oidc/token endpoint as other grants and binds audience via the resource parameter. For token_exchange_wrong_audience and token_exchange_ignore_audience tests, the fuzzer MUST vary resource exactly and compare resulting aud claims or rejection behavior; do not assume a separate audience parameter exists beyond resource semantics.

OIDC endpoints in Logto require application/x-www-form-urlencoded for token, revocation, and introspection requests. Sending JSON may fail for protocol reasons unrelated to security. The fuzzer MUST use form encoding for /oidc/token, /oidc/token/revocation, and /oidc/token/introspection.

Current Logto SDK sign-out behavior is effectively global sign-out: it clears the centralized Logto session via /session/end flow. However, if offline_access was granted, the app grant may remain until grant TTL expiry. Therefore, a successful end-session does NOT guarantee refresh-token invalidation. The fuzzer MUST test revocation separately from browser session logout.

Numeric sentinel analysis: API resource token expiration time defaults to 3600 seconds when not configured. The documentation does not define 0 as 'immediate expiry' or 'disable'; the fuzzer MUST NOT assume 0 is a safe sentinel. Treat omitted expiration as default 3600 and test explicit low TTLs only when the API actually documents them.

Numeric sentinel analysis: personal access token one-time token/magic link expiration defaults to 10 minutes when expiresIn is omitted. The docs do not define 0 or -1 as disable/strict sentinels. The fuzzer MUST NOT assume 0 disables expiry or means immediate expiration unless the specific API endpoint documents it.

OIDC SSO/direct sign-in tests must still start at /oidc/auth. Direct sign-in is only a user-flow parameter that skips the hosted page and redirects to the configured IdP; it is not an API login bypass. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat direct_sign_in as a standalone authentication API.

The resource parameter uses EXACT string matching only. Documentation states the resource parameter must exactly match the registered API identifier (resource indicator URI). For I5 audience tests, do not use prefixes, shortened values, or wildcard-like patterns; they will not match. For multi-resource scenarios, request each exact resource URI explicitly.

Scope/permission names use EXACT string matching only. Documentation explicitly says scope names must exactly match permission names and prefixes/shortened versions do not work as wildcards. For I5 tests, the fuzzer MUST request exact scope strings; for multi-permission scenarios, enumerate all needed scopes explicitly rather than using patterns.

For organization-scoped JWT tests, organization RBAC is applied only when organization_id is included in the token request. If organization_id is omitted, only global roles/permissions are evaluated. The fuzzer MUST include organization_id when testing organization permissions or organization-level API resources, and MUST omit it when testing purely global authorization behavior.

Organization permissions and global API permissions are distinct models and cannot be mixed in a single authorization expectation. The fuzzer MUST not interpret a token lacking organization_id as evidence that organization RBAC failed; by design, Logto evaluates only global roles in that case.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against Logto-issued JWTs, include a CONTROL flow that obtains a valid token from the same tenant and resource first. Without a control, a failed protected-resource call may reflect missing resource/scope/organization configuration rather than freshness enforcement.

Logto documentation examples in several languages disable automatic audience verification in JWT libraries (verify_aud: false / ValidateAudience = false) and instruct applications to verify audience manually based on the permission model. Therefore, when testing I1/I5 audience binding, the fuzzer MUST validate the aud claim itself against the requested resource or organization audience and MUST NOT assume library defaults enforce audience checks.

For organization-level API tokens, the API must validate BOTH audience and organization context. The fuzzer MUST check aud matches the API resource indicator and organization_id matches the expected organization. Accepting only one of these is insufficient and can cause false negatives in tenant-isolation tests.

Logto does not support fetching organization tokens directly from the authorization code flow. To obtain an organization token for user-based tests, the fuzzer MUST first obtain a refresh token, then call /oidc/token with grant_type=refresh_token plus organization parameters. Treating the initial authorization_code token response as the final organization token will misconfigure tests.

An access token can only include scopes that were requested in the original OAuth authorization flow. For I5 scope-escalation tests, the fuzzer MUST compare granted scopes against the original requested scope set and MUST NOT expect refresh or later issuance to add scopes that were never requested.

Token exchange is disabled by default per application. Before running PAT or impersonation token_exchange tests, the target application MUST have 'Allow token exchange' enabled, otherwise failures are expected configuration errors rather than security behavior.

PAT token exchange and refresh-token-derived access tokens are documented as equivalent in authorization behavior. The fuzzer MUST treat successful PAT exchange as by-design and compare resulting scopes/audience/organization context against the same authorization rules as refresh-token issuance, not as a separate privilege-escalation path by itself.

For token_exchange tests, subject_token_type must be set to the exact documented token type. For PAT exchange use urn:logto:token-type:personal_access_token; using a different type is a setup error, not a security result. For impersonation examples, subject_token_type is urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token.

Logto-issued JWTs are signed with tenant signing keys exposed at /oidc/jwks, and signing key rotation changes trust immediately in Cloud but requires restart in OSS. For I3 signing-key-rotation tests, only acceptance of OLD keys after explicit rotation is suspicious; acceptance of NEW keys after admin rotation is by design. On OSS, allow for restart requirement before judging propagation.

Never rotate signing keys consecutively during tests. Documentation warns that consecutive rotations may invalidate all issued tokens. The fuzzer MUST perform at most one rotation per scenario and avoid interpreting mass token invalidation after repeated rotations as a broker vulnerability.

Logto supports direct_sign_in as a user-flow parameter only through the authorization endpoint. The fuzzer MUST still initiate authentication via GET /oidc/auth and MUST NOT treat direct sign-in as a direct API login bypass. If the connector is missing or disabled, fallback to the standard sign-in page is by design.

For OIDC request construction, ui_locales is a space-separated BCP 47 list and Logto picks the first supported tag. This affects UI and downstream email localization only for the current interaction. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat language-dependent output differences as identity or authorization mismatches.

Logto does not support Resource Owner Password Credentials and requires redirect-based OIDC flows for user authentication. Therefore login_with_password is absent for oidc_jwt user flows by design; the fuzzer MUST use start_oidc_auth plus exchange_code_for_token (or client_credentials/token_exchange where documented) instead of attempting direct username/password token requests.

Logto's /oidc/token endpoint uses application/x-www-form-urlencoded for authorization_code, refresh_token, client_credentials, and token_exchange requests. The fuzzer MUST send form-encoded bodies, not JSON, for exchange_code_for_token and token_exchange.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against Logto-issued JWTs, include a CONTROL token flow in the same setup using a valid token request and then compare outcomes. A failed attack request alone cannot distinguish token-validation behavior from broken client/app/resource configuration.

Audience/resource matching is exact. The resource parameter in authorization and token requests MUST exactly match the registered API identifier (resource indicator URI). Do NOT use prefixes, shortened forms, or wildcard-like values; they are not documented as pattern matches.

Scope/permission matching is exact string match only. Logto documentation states scope names must exactly match permission names defined on the API resource; prefixes and shortened versions do not work as wildcards. For I5 tests, do NOT assume partial or wildcard scope matching.

When testing JWT-vs-opaque-token behavior, remember that Logto issues an opaque access token when no resource is specified. To obtain a JWT access token for API validation tests, the fuzzer MUST request a resource (or rely on a configured default API resource). Otherwise verify_granted_identity via /oidc/me may work with an opaque token and JWT-specific checks become inapplicable.

For organization token tests, Logto does not support fetching organization tokens directly from the authorization code flow. The fuzzer MUST first obtain a refresh token, then call /oidc/token with grant_type=refresh_token plus organization parameters, or use client_credentials with organization_id. Do NOT expect organization-scoped JWTs directly from the initial code exchange.

For organization-level API and organization-permission tests, organization RBAC is only applied when organization_id is included in the token request. If organization_id is omitted, only global roles/permissions are evaluated. The fuzzer MUST include organization_id when testing organization isolation or organization-scoped authorization.

For global API permission-change tests, enlarged permissions do NOT appear through refresh unless they were part of the originally requested scope set. A valid I3/I5 enlargement test must run a new authorization flow when requesting newly granted scopes outside the original request; refresh alone is insufficient.

For downscoping tests, existing JWTs keep old scopes until expiry. The fuzzer MUST obtain a newly issued token after role/permission changes before asserting reduced permissions. Reusing an old token after admin changes is BY DESIGN and not evidence of stale authorization enforcement.

Token exchange is disabled by default per application. Before running RFC 8693 token_exchange tests, the target application MUST have 'Allow token exchange' enabled, otherwise failures are expected setup errors rather than security behavior.

For PAT or impersonation token_exchange tests, subject_token_type is exact and grant-specific. PAT exchange requires subject_token_type=urn:logto:token-type:personal_access_token. Impersonation examples use subject_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token. The fuzzer MUST use the documented exact token type string for the scenario under test.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, Logto documents that exchanged access tokens obtained from PATs behave identically to refresh-token-derived tokens, but scope inclusion still follows normal token request semantics. The fuzzer SHOULD compare requested scope vs returned scope and MUST NOT assume omitted scope means full upstream permissions.

For OIDC login flow tests, Logto supports PKCE and its SDK/core conventions require code_challenge_method=S256. The fuzzer SHOULD use PKCE in start_oidc_auth and exchange_code_for_token sequences to match documented secure flow behavior.

For direct sign-in tests, direct_sign_in values are exact-format strings: social:<idp-name> for social connectors and sso:<connector-id> for enterprise SSO. If the connector is not found or not enabled, Logto falls back to the standard sign-in page. The fuzzer MUST treat fallback-to-login-page as a setup issue, not as successful direct provider binding.

For sign-out and session-coherence tests, current Logto SDK signOut behavior performs global end-session at /oidc/session/end and may preserve grants when offline_access was granted. The fuzzer MUST distinguish centralized Logto session revocation from grant/refresh-token revocation; a user may be signed out of browser SSO while refresh-token-backed grants remain valid until grant expiry.

Grant lifetime is long-lived by default (180 days) and offline_access grants are not revoked by end-session. For I2/I3 tests involving logout or session invalidation, do NOT assume end-session revokes refresh-token capability. Explicit revocation or grant expiry is required to invalidate offline_access-backed renewal.
Logto's OIDC UserInfo endpoint is /oidc/me, not /userinfo. The fuzzer MUST use /oidc/me for verify_granted_identity on this platform.

OIDC discovery is available at /oidc/.well-known/openid-configuration and exposes issuer and jwks_uri. For I1 trust-anchor and issuer-validation tests against Logto-issued tokens, the fuzzer SHOULD derive issuer and JWKS from discovery rather than hardcoding mismatched values.

environment_defaults.api_pattern: Logto Management API uses /api/ prefix. User CRUD: /api/users. SSO connectors: /api/sso-connectors. Applications: /api/applications.
environment_defaults.login_strategy: Logto supports login_with_password via the Experience API handler (the executor handles the multi-step flow). For M2M service login, use login_with_jwt with client_credentials grant.
environment_defaults.app_types: Logto application types: Native, SPA, Traditional, MachineToMachine, Protected, SAML. Do NOT use TraditionalWeb or WebApp — use 'Traditional'.
environment_defaults.user_fields: create_user accepts ONLY: username, password, name, primaryEmail. Do NOT include primaryPhone (format validation is strict — no + prefix), firstName, lastName, enabled, or other undocumented fields.
